exposure: serum Vitamin-D (VD) levels (deficient < 20 ng/ml vs. sufficient > 20 ng/ml)
cohort: Sixty pregnant patients from Samsun Medikalpark Hospital whose serum VD levels were measured at 24 weeks of gestation and who subsequently underwent cesarean section.
finding: The amniotic fluid NF-kB concentration was significantly lower in the VD sufficient group compared to the VD deficient group, indicating that VD insufficiency causes early inflammatory changes in fetal membranes, but it does not lead to preterm delivery.
cross-section timing: Serum VD levels were measured at 24 weeks of gestation; amniotic fluid NF-kB levels were measured during cesarean section.
